records.severitySource: NHS: Taking paracetamol with other medicines (do not take with other paracetamol-containing medicines)
records.action: Official UK information: count every product; no more than 4 g in 24 hours for an adult.

evidence.title: NHS: Taking paracetamol for adults with other medicines and herbal supplements
NHS: Common questions about paracetamol for adults
evidence.section: What if I take too much?

records.bName: Enzyme-inducing medicines (carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin, St John's wort)
records.mechanismNote: Induction of CYP2E1 and CYP3A4 increases NAPQI formation
records.effect: Carbamazepine, phenytoin, rifampicin and other enzyme-inducing drugs increase the toxic metabolite of paracetamol and the risk of liver injury, particularly in overdose.
records.sourceWording: The BNF lists enzyme inducers among drugs that may increase the risk of paracetamol hepatotoxicity.
records.severitySource: BNF: Paracetamol interactions (increased risk of hepatotoxicity with enzyme inducers)
records.action: Documented; keep within the recommended dose and seek advice about the lower toxic threshold after any overdose.

evidence.title: NHS: Taking paracetamol for adults with other medicines and herbal supplements

records.mechanismNote: CYP2C19 inhibition blocks conversion of clopidogrel to its active metabolite
records.effect: Omeprazole reduces the activation of clopidogrel, which may make it less effective at preventing clots after a stent or heart attack.
records.sourceWording: UK information lists clopidogrel among medicines that omeprazole can affect; the BNF advises avoiding the combination and using an alternative PPI.
records.severitySource: BNF: Omeprazole interactions (reduced antiplatelet effect of clopidogrel; avoid)
records.action: Official UK guidance: avoid; lansoprazole or pantoprazole are preferred alternatives when acid suppression is needed with clopidogrel.

evidence.title: NHS: Taking omeprazole with other medicines and herbal supplements
MedlinePlus: Omeprazole
evidence.section: What special precautions should I follow?

records.effect: Proton pump inhibitors can reduce the elimination of methotrexate and raise its levels, most importantly with high-dose methotrexate.
records.sourceWording: UK information lists methotrexate among medicines to tell a doctor about; the BNF advises considering withholding the PPI around high-dose methotrexate.
records.severitySource: BNF: Omeprazole interactions (increased methotrexate concentration; consider withholding with high dose)
records.action: Official guidance: the PPI may be withheld around high-dose methotrexate; low-dose weekly methotrexate is monitored.

evidence.title: NHS: Taking omeprazole with other medicines and herbal supplements
MedlinePlus: Omeprazole
evidence.section: What special precautions should I follow?

records.mechanismNote: Inhibition of CYP2C19 slows clearance of the less active R-warfarin
records.effect: Omeprazole can raise the INR in people taking warfarin.
records.sourceWording: UK information lists warfarin among medicines omeprazole can interact with and advises telling a doctor; the BNF advises monitoring the INR.
records.severitySource: BNF: Omeprazole interactions (enhanced anticoagulant effect; monitor INR)
records.action: Official guidance: INR checked after starting or stopping omeprazole.

evidence.title: NHS: Taking omeprazole with other medicines and herbal supplements

records.effect: Omeprazole greatly reduces the absorption of the HIV medicine rilpivirine, which can lead to treatment failure.
records.sourceWording: The BNF lists rilpivirine as a contraindication to omeprazole.
records.severitySource: BNF: Omeprazole contra-indications (rilpivirine)
records.action: Official guidance: contraindicated; an H2 antagonist or antacid with appropriate timing is used instead.

evidence.title: NHS: Taking omeprazole with other medicines and herbal supplements

records.effect: Omeprazole can modestly raise digoxin levels by increasing its absorption.
records.sourceWording: UK information lists digoxin among medicines to tell a doctor about; the BNF advises monitoring digoxin levels, particularly in older people.
records.severitySource: BNF: Omeprazole interactions (increased digoxin concentration; monitor)
records.action: Official guidance: digoxin levels and symptoms of toxicity monitored.

evidence.title: NHS: Taking omeprazole with other medicines and herbal supplements

records.effect: Reduced stomach acid lowers the absorption of levothyroxine, which can leave thyroid replacement inadequate.
records.sourceWording: The BNF lists proton pump inhibitors among drugs that may reduce levothyroxine absorption and advises monitoring.
records.severitySource: BNF: Levothyroxine interactions (reduced absorption with PPIs; monitor)
records.action: Official guidance: TSH rechecked after starting a PPI; the levothyroxine dose adjusted if needed.

evidence.title: NHS: Taking levothyroxine with other medicines and herbal supplements

records.mechanismNote: Altered gut flora and vitamin K availability
records.effect: Amoxicillin can raise the INR in people on warfarin, probably by altering the gut bacteria that make vitamin K.
records.sourceWording: UK information lists warfarin among medicines to tell a doctor about when prescribed amoxicillin; the BNF advises monitoring the INR.
records.severitySource: BNF: Amoxicillin interactions (possible enhanced anticoagulant effect; monitor INR)
records.action: Official guidance: extra INR checks during and after the course.

records.effect: Penicillins reduce the kidney's excretion of methotrexate, raising its levels and toxicity.

records.severitySource: BNF: Amoxicillin interactions (reduced methotrexate excretion; monitor)
records.action: Official guidance: monitored for methotrexate toxicity during the course, or an alternative antibiotic chosen.

records.effect: Allopurinol with amoxicillin increases the chance of a skin rash.
records.sourceWording: UK information lists allopurinol among medicines to tell a doctor about because of the increased risk of rash.

records.action: Documented; a rash during the course is reported and assessed rather than assumed to be penicillin allergy.

records.effect: Antibiotics inactivate the live oral typhoid vaccine.
records.sourceWording: The BNF advises avoiding antibacterials for 3 days before and after the oral typhoid vaccine.
records.severitySource: BNF: Amoxicillin interactions (oral typhoid vaccine inactivated; avoid)
records.action: Official guidance: the vaccine is given at least 3 days before or after an antibiotic course.

records.effect: Azithromycin can raise the INR and bleeding risk in people on warfarin.

records.effect: Antacids containing aluminium or magnesium reduce the peak level of azithromycin.
records.sourceWording: US information advises taking azithromycin at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after antacids containing aluminium or magnesium hydroxide.

records.effect: Azithromycin with other medicines that prolong the QT interval (amiodarone, sotalol, some antipsychotics and antidepressants, quinolone antibiotics, ondansetron) increases the risk of dangerous heart rhythms.
records.sourceWording: US information advises telling a doctor about medicines for irregular heartbeat and other listed drugs, whose doses may need changing or monitoring; the BNF advises caution or avoidance depending on the drug.
records.severitySource: MedlinePlus: Azithromycin precautions (doses may need changing or monitoring with these medicines)
records.action: Official information: an alternative antibiotic where possible; otherwise ECG and electrolyte monitoring.
records.population: Higher risk with heart disease, bradycardia, low potassium or magnesium, older age

records.effect: Two macrolide antibiotics together (azithromycin with clarithromycin or erythromycin) add QT prolongation and gut side effects without benefit.
records.sourceWording: Macrolides share cautions on QT prolongation; guidance never combines them.
records.severitySource: BNF: Clarithromycin cautions (QT prolongation); therapeutic duplication
records.action: One macrolide at a time.

ace-inhibitors.text: Two ACE inhibitors together, or an ACE inhibitor with an ARB, duplicate renin-angiotensin blockade and increase the risk of kidney injury, hyperkalaemia and hypotension without extra benefit.

source.title: NICE NG136: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management

angiotensin-receptor-blockers.text: An ARB with another ARB or with an ACE inhibitor duplicates renin-angiotensin blockade; UK guidance advises against combining them for hypertension.

source.title: NICE NG136: Hypertension in adults: diagnosis and management

beta-blockers.text: Two beta blockers together offer no benefit and add bradycardia and hypotension.

statins.text: Two statins together add muscle and liver toxicity without additional benefit; combinations for extra LDL lowering use ezetimibe or other classes instead.

source.title: NICE NG238: Cardiovascular disease: risk assessment and reduction, including lipid modification

anticoagulants.text: Two anticoagulants together (for example warfarin with a DOAC outside a supervised switch) multiply bleeding risk and are avoided.

antiplatelets.text: Aspirin with another antiplatelet (dual antiplatelet therapy) is a deliberate, time-limited prescription after stents and acute coronary syndromes; taking two antiplatelets without such an indication adds bleeding risk.

nsaids.text: Two NSAIDs together (including aspirin at pain-relief doses, or an oral NSAID with a prescription NSAID such as naproxen) add gastrointestinal, kidney and cardiovascular harm without extra pain relief; UK information advises not taking ibuprofen with similar painkillers without advice.

source.title: NHS: Taking ibuprofen for adults with other medicines and herbal supplements

non-opioid-analgesics.text: Paracetamol is present in many cold remedies and combination painkillers (co-codamol, co-dydramol); taking more than one product containing it risks overdose. UK information advises checking labels and not combining paracetamol products.

source.title: NHS: Taking paracetamol for adults with other medicines and herbal supplements

opioids.text: Two opioids together (for example codeine in a combination product with a prescribed strong opioid) add sedation and respiratory depression; combinations are prescribed deliberately, never added over the counter.

proton-pump-inhibitors.text: Two PPIs together, or a PPI with an over-the-counter omeprazole product, duplicate acid suppression and its long-term risks.

ssris.text: Two SSRIs together, or an SSRI with another serotonergic antidepressant, raise the risk of serotonin syndrome; switching is done with a planned cross-taper.

macrolides.text: Two macrolides together add QT prolongation and gut side effects without benefit.

products.name: Co-codamol
products.note: Paracetamol with codeine; 8/500 strength available from UK pharmacies, higher strengths on prescription. Counts towards the daily paracetamol total.

products.name: Co-amoxiclav
products.note: Amoxicillin with the beta-lactamase inhibitor clavulanic acid; carries amoxicillin's allergy profile plus a risk of cholestatic jaundice.

products.name: Nurofen Plus
products.note: Ibuprofen with codeine, pharmacy-only in the UK for short-term use.

products.name: Anadin Extra
products.note: A combination painkiller containing both aspirin and paracetamol; counts towards both totals.

products.name: Lemsip Max
aliases: cold and flu remedies with paracetamol
products.note: One of many cold and flu remedies containing paracetamol; the commonest source of accidental paracetamol duplication.

products.name: Tylenol PM
products.note: Acetaminophen (paracetamol) with the sedating antihistamine diphenhydramine.

products.name: Exforge
products.note: Amlodipine with the ARB valsartan; carries the interactions of both.

products.name: Caduet
products.note: Amlodipine with atorvastatin in one tablet.

products.name: Cozaar-Comp
products.note: Losartan with a thiazide diuretic; adds low potassium and sodium and gout to losartan's own cautions.

products.name: Janumet
products.note: Metformin with the DPP-4 inhibitor sitagliptin; all metformin cautions apply.

products.name: Entresto
products.note: A heart-failure medicine that must never be combined with an ACE inhibitor (36-hour washout) because of angioedema.

products.name: Zegerid
products.note: Immediate-release omeprazole buffered with sodium bicarbonate.
